steps.text: Mix together brown sugar, sage, salt, black pepper, marjoram, red pepper flakes, and cloves in a small bowl until well combined.
Place pork in a large bowl. Add spice mixture and mix with your hands until well combined. Form mixture into 6 patties.

Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add patties and cook until browned and crispy, about 5 minutes per side. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the center should read at least 160 degrees F (71 degrees C).

raw_recipe.headline: Homemade Breakfast Sausage
raw_recipe.description: Homemade breakfast sausage patties made with ground pork, brown sugar, and sage deliver sweet and savory flavor in every bite. Serve alongside eggs or in a breakfast sandwich!

video.description: The homemade breakfast sausage patties in this video are made with ground pork, brown sugar, and sage deliver sweet and savory flavor in every bite. These are better than store-bought since you can flavor them as you like! Serve a patty alongside scrambled eggs and hash brown potatoes or layer one with a fried egg and a slice of cheese to make a tasty breakfast sandwich.

review.reviewBody:
Like other reviewers, I was in search of a recipe to make breakfast sausage since I cannot have many of the additives (mostly MSG) in commercially-prepared sausage. We moved and I could no longer find sausage without additives.

Even if you *can* eat commercial sausage, DON'T - make this and you'll never make anything else!!! I used 1/2 ground pork and 1/2 fresh ground turkey (better texture than frozen). This cuts the fat content, and it's still so great! I made the recipe as stated, but next time I'll cut down on the sage and increase the red pepper to our own liking. My family doesn't want to eat anything else now! The first Sunday I cooked the sausage for breakfast, my husband said he just kept thinking about how good it was all during church service!

If you haven't tried Lee Fogle's Italian Sausage recipe - YOU MUST! It's also fantastic! THANK YOU!!!!

Have been fumbling around for the best sausage recipe. Wow! Just made this recipe and tried some left over scraps. Substituted 1 1/2 tsp fennel seed for the clove (which I did not have). Rolled the sausage out to about 3/8" between two layers of waxed paper and plastic wrap (to protect my wooden roller). Cut out rounds with a three inch biscuit cutter. Reroll and cut out until only a few scraps are left. It made 18 rounds with some scraps for tasting. Oh Yum!

I ground up 9lbs of pork shoulder (pork butt/Boston Butt) which has plenty of fat in it. I did not experience this being dry at all. I used the ingredients in the exact quantities mentioned and found this to be some of the most flavorful sausage I’ve had. (I did leave out the red pepper flakes) I’ve been wanting to make my own breakfast sausage since getting my grinder and thought I’d start with this recipe and tweak as needed. Well no tweaking required!! I love it as is. I may make some spicy sausage in the future by adding the red pepper flakes, but for now this is great!! I did separate out 4lbs of the sausage and added a nice maple syrup at the quantity of 1/8C per lb, or 1/2C For the full 4 lbs. that’s ALSO really good! Should be stocked up on sausage for awhile! Thank You for sharing!

With the tweaks suggested by other users these were SO GOOD! I doubled everything except the salt and the meat. For the red pepper flakes I did a heaping ⅛ tsp. OH I completely omitted the clove and added a pinch of fennel seeds instead. I then rolled the meat out to ⅜ of an inch and cut them out with my donut cutter that was slightly larger than my English muffins. Got 8 patties this way and omg! I just wanted to try a little nibble of one and ended up eating the whole thing plain. This recipe is going in my recipe book.

I use this recipe for pork or chicken sausage. For chicken, I dice up boneless thighs, put them in the food processor with all of the seasoning with a little olive oil. Just spin it until blended. Really tasty and healthy.

Great recipe! The seasonings were spot on.
I used the paddle attachment on my Kitchen Aid to blend all the ingredients together. I then made patties with my burger press, pre-cooked them, then froze to make quick and easy breakfasts and breakfast sandwiches.
Thanks for sharing.

We love this recipe! I added 1tsp thyme,a pinch of oregano, and substituted nutmeg for the cloves. I also had to add some sweet potato scraps to make it 2 lbs. I rolled it out like another comment said and got 18 patties. I have 12 patties flash freezing right now for later. I cut our own sweet potato fries and flash freeze them. The smaller pieces I put in a separate freezer bag and become my scraps for later. That's what I used. Since I've learned to flash freeze things we've saved so much. I also ground pork chops for this recipe. Best investment is a grinder

Just made these this morning from pork shoulder. Loved the flavor. Didn’t add Marjoram because I didn’t have any. To get a thin Patty, I put two lbs in a gallon size bag and mashed it down untouched an even layer. With the bag closed I scored the pork into 8 rectangle. Made two patties and maybe my heat was too high, because they were dry. Need tips on cooking them, because the flavor was spot on.

Excellent basic recipe. I like sage and the stuff is fluffy anyway so I doubled it. I'd go further on the red pepper flakes to taste. And I used brownulated brown sugar. Mix spices and salt thoroughly and distribute evenly over meat before mixing it in. Try cooking a small patty and tasting to adjust seasonings.

I followed the advice of others that said to double the spices and it was perfect. I also wanted to double the recipe - we took these camping -for easy breakfast as I precooked them. Then froze them! I only had ground chicken so I Used that with the ground pork. I felt that lightened them up a little and I’ll do that next time...there will def be a next time. My family and friends loved them. I also baked them. Perfect.
I used only 18oz pork trim, subbed oregano for marjoram, blended in my food processor and finished with 2 oz ice cubes. Wonderful!

I don’t even like pork sausage and these were so delicious. Knowing there’s no nitrates or preservatives makes them even more yummy. These patties will definitely be a staple in our household for now on. 😋

I made the recipe exactly as written for 2 pounds of ground pork, and it came out amazing. I was worried that it would be under seasoned, but it was perfect. Exactly what I was looking for in this recipe.

On their own, these were WAY too salty for me ( I dunked bites into maple syrup to balance it :) . I'll cut it in half next time. Overall, we did enjoy them and it was a solid first attempt at homemade sausage.
I love this recipe! Although I also get much more than 6 patties since I like them thinner but they are still pretty big, I kinda eyeball the amount for each one, this time I got 14 patties
This was so easy and delicious. I didn't make patties out of it. Instead, I left it as a crumble and made breakfast burritos. Even my fussy husband loved it!
I only used 1 lb of pork (since there is only 2 of us) and halved the salt but kept the remaining ingredients the same and it was awesome!
Super easy recipe to make and turned out amazing. Such great flavors
I didn’t add the Marjoram because I didn’t have any and they tasted wonderful!
I make this every week. It is delicious and I can avoid preservatives. I skip the brown sugar since I am watching my sugar intake, still delicious.
